messages.subject: preddata with ArcGis
parts:
Hello,

I am currently trying to do a DSM model and to do so I need to obtain the preddata table. I just created a grid via the Fishnet tool of ArcMap which had the same columns, rows and cell size that my raster containing the covariates information  (from Bio Oracle). By doing so I obtained a table containing 7257600 points which seems like a lot in comparison with the 1374 of the mexdolphins dataset, so my question is: how do you determine the resolution of the grid? 

Thanks for your help,

Julia

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] preddata with ArcGis
parts:
Hi Julia, listfolk,

The question of how large to make the prediction grid cells is common in
DSM methodology and I don't have a complete answer (others should
obviously chime in if they have other thoughts...) My feeling is this
probably heavily depends on the animals your studying and the area in
which you study them.

Two general thoughts:

I think the main issue to be aware of is the resolution of the grid on
which your covariates live: it's possible in Arc and other packages to
interpolate to fine scales -- this may not be advisable (depending on
your covariates. So, sticking to scales similar to those that the data
were collected on seems sensible. Conversely, going much bigger may
average out interesting or troublesome patterns in the covariates, which
you may view as negative or positive. (Recent work of Foster et al 2012
and Stoklosa et al 2015 highlight this kind of issue, though don't
directly address what we're talking about here.)

Secondly, sticking on a scale the size of the segments in your data or
larger also seems prudent, as the model doesn't know more about the
distribution of the animals in question than at the scale of the segments.

My plan is to run some simulations to check my thoughts above in the
near future, should I get around to that I will post to this list as
there has been previous interest in this topic.

If anyone else has experience or has seen relevant literature on this
topic, please do post this here!



Hope this helps!
--dave



References:

Foster, S.D., Shimadzu, H. & Darnell, R. (2012) Uncertainty in spatially
predicted covariates: is it ignorable? Journal of the Royal Statistical
Society, Series C, 61, 637–652.

Stoklosa, J., Daly, C., Foster, S. D., Ashcroft, M. B., Warton, D. I.
(2015), A climate of uncertainty: accounting for error in climate
variables for species distribution models. Methods in Ecology and
Evolution, 6: 412–423. doi: 10.1111/2041-210X.12217
